Caris Life Sciences.why: its revenue is Whole Exome / Whole Transcriptome molecular profiling read by AI models trained on its own clinico-genomic database (over 1.13 million profiled cases), plus pharma R&D services built on that data, so wider use of AI-driven precision oncology and its new AI-based assays (Caris Detect, MRD) drives its sales
Caris Life Sciences.evidence: Caris Life Sciences Q2 FY2026 call (08-05-2026): CEO - 'we've built one of the deepest molecular databases in all of oncology, over 1.13 million patients and the AI trained on that'; Q2 total revenue $263.7 million, up 45%, with molecular profiling services revenue $252.3 million

players.product: whole-exome / whole-transcriptome molecular profiling (MI Profile tissue, Caris Assure blood), clinico-genomic database and AI models

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (CEO: a record quarter with record clinical volume): total revenue increased 45% year-over-year to $263.7 million. Molecular profiling services revenue was $252.3 million, up 55%, and pharma R&D services revenue was $11.4 million, reflecting the timing of deliverables as the company focuses on longer-term partnerships rather than one-time smaller deals. Revenue growth was driven by volume growth of 18% and a 30% increase in clinical ASP.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $263.7M (+45%); molecular profiling $252.3M (+55%); pharma R&D $11.4M; volume +18%; clinical ASP +30%

quarterly_data.signal: GAAP gross margin expanded to 68% from 63% a year ago and 65% last quarter; operating expenses were $152.7 million, up about $21 million year-over-year on commercial expansion and the product pipeline including Caris Detect. GAAP net loss narrowed to $0.6 million, including a $25 million one-time extinguishment charge for the April term-loan refinancing. Adjusted EBITDA was $55.7 million (vs $16.7 million a year ago) and EBITDA about $33 million; net cash from operations was $28.5 million and free cash flow $6.4 million after $22.1 million of capex, the fifth consecutive quarter of positive adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow. Cash and investments were $793 million at quarter end.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP gross margin 68%; opex $152.7M; net loss $0.6M; adjusted EBITDA $55.7M (vs $16.7M); FCF $6.4M; capex $22.1M; cash and investments $793M

quarterly_data.signal: Clinical case volume grew from approximately 52,800 cases in Q1 to approximately 59,200 in Q2, up 18% year-over-year and 12% sequentially; the roughly 6,400 incremental cases were a company record (CFO: still a record excluding the about 1,000 cases that rolled over from Q1). MI Profile tissue cases were approximately 48,300 (+13% YoY, +11% sequentially) and Caris Assure blood cases 10,700 (+50% YoY, +17% sequentially). CEO: 'Last quarter, we ran over 345,000 clinical oncology tests, including over 114,000 Whole Exome and Whole Transcriptome tests.' It supports more than 6,200 ordering oncologists, with more than 74% of orders coming through EHR and portal channels (CFO: just above 50% in Q1 last year). CFO: the blood-tissue attach rate (cases with blood in addition to tissue) has been consistent in the roughly 40% range historically.
quarterly_data.figure: ~59,200 cases (+18% YoY, +12% QoQ); tissue ~48,300 (+13%); blood 10,700 (+50%); >345,000 tests; >114,000 WES/WTS tests; >6,200 ordering oncologists; >74% orders via EHR/portal

quarterly_data.signal: The Caris dataset surpassed 1.13 million profiled cases, including more than 733,000 Whole Exomes, 783,000 Transcriptomes and approximately 843,000 matched cases with clinical outcomes. CEO: Caris is now putting its AI directly in customers' hands with large language models and a next-generation AI assistant called JAKE, with which they can run comparative analyses against the proprietary database. The Precision Oncology Alliance reached 101 members, adding UC San Francisco and Northwell Health this quarter. CEO: the same sequencing, database and AI engine is expected to extend over time into other disease areas, including cardiology, neurology and autoimmune.
quarterly_data.figure: >1.13M profiled cases; >733,000 Whole Exomes; 783,000 Transcriptomes; ~843,000 matched cases with outcomes; 101 Precision Oncology Alliance members

quarterly_data.signal: Blended clinical ASP surpassed $3,850, a company record, and the company will disclose only the blended clinical ASP going forward. Approximately 75% of MI Profile volume is MI CancerSeq. Covered lives stand at approximately 239.5 million for MI CancerSeq and 131.9 million for Caris Assure (CFO: its coverage strategy is expected to play out into 2027). CFO: the reimbursement position is viewed as stable, with an expected update in September on the current PAMA reporting cycle; CEO: 'We're expecting a pricing increase with PAMA.' CFO: the bulk of prior-period collections were in tissue profiling, and these true-ups are getting smaller as a percent of revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: blended ASP >$3,850 (record); covered lives ~239.5M (MI CancerSeq), 131.9M (Caris Assure); ~75% of MI Profile volume is MI CancerSeq

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 outlook raised: total revenue of $1.03 billion to $1.04 billion (27% to 28% growth), up from $1.0 billion to $1.02 billion, driven by molecular profiling strength; clinical therapy selection volume growth of approximately 20% maintained, with Q3 expected to hit that mark; GAAP operating expenses of $595 million to $600 million (from $590 million to $595 million) on commercial expansion and launch marketing; adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow positive for the full year. The guidance assumes nothing for Caris Detect, the pending New York State approval or second-half true-ups; the CFO confirmed the full-year pharma R&D framework of $75 million to $80 million still holds.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $1.03B-$1.04B (+27%-28%), prior $1.0B-$1.02B; therapy selection volume ~+20%; GAAP opex $595M-$600M; pharma R&D $75M-$80M

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 outlook (CFO): the 20% volume-growth target equates to roughly 61,000 to 62,000 cases; blended ASP roughly $3,800 to $3,900; EBITDA about $10 million to $16 million, then maybe improving in Q4 back up to the Q2 level; capex of $15 million to $20 million; free cash flow basically neutral for the first nine months as the $30-ish million of H1 free cash flow funds the inventory ramp and Caris Detect initiatives, then positive again in Q4. Gross margin is expected in the mid-to-high 60% range in H2 and the tissue/blood mix perhaps 79/21 (80/20 range historically). Pharma revenue is expected to improve from Q2 to Q3, with Q4 typically heavier.

CEO: current capacity is about $1 billion a year of revenue and is about to triple to about $3 billion a year, 'and we're still worried about back orders'; near-term Caris Detect demand may run ahead of the rollout. Inventory increased $47 million from Q1 to Q2, built on purpose ahead of expected Detect volume, and Q2 capex of $22.1 million went to ramping capacity for the new product launches. President: capacity is being expanded aggressively, and it is quite likely it will not stay above demand.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity ~$1B a year of revenue, tripling to ~$3B; inventory +$47M QoQ; Q2 capex $22.1M

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Caris is looking at additional sequencing capabilities beyond its current existing supplier, with incremental capex dollars in H2 2026. President: two competitors are now out there against the long-standing sequencing supplier, with significantly higher throughput and lower cost, creating the opportunity to increase Caris's capacity and decrease its cost of goods simultaneously. CFO: new sequencing technologies that could reduce COGS further are being assessed; the approach remains 'deeper, not cheaper' at launch, then driving costs down with scale.

Caris Detect, a multi-cancer early detection blood test built on ultra-deep Whole Genome Sequencing together with cell-free RNA, launched in June 2026 and identifies 58 distinct cancer types from a single blood draw. In validation: 60% Stage I/II sensitivity, and across a little over 2,500 true positives the tissue-of-origin classifier resolved 83.9% in a single workup and 99.8% within two (an average of 1.19 procedures per patient). It goes the self-pay route (CFO: no reimbursement plans right now) and is sold mostly through channel partners (President), with strong interest from many potential channel partners in concierge medicine, longevity centers and digital platforms such as Everlywell, backed by a national direct-to-consumer ad campaign starting in a couple of months. CFO: Detect COGS is expected to be consistent with the existing liquid product's gross margins; nothing for Detect is in guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: 58 cancer types; 60% Stage I/II sensitivity; 83.9% resolved in one workup, 99.8% within two; 1.19 procedures per patient
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: potential channel partner (Caris Detect digital platform)

quarterly_data.signal: MRD: President - Caris will finish validation and look to launch MRD in the back half of 2026, with two approaches: a tumor-naive Whole Exome plus Whole Transcriptome assay on the Caris Assure platform, initially in Stage 2 and 3 colorectal cancer, for which longitudinal outcome data are being collected for a MolDX technical assessment (probably another six months at least of clinical maturity needed), and a tumor-informed Whole Genome assay on the Caris Precision platform for pan-tumor Stage 1 through 3, with a median of roughly 15,000 trackers per patient, over five logs of linear dynamic range and an R-squared above 0.99.
quarterly_data.figure: MRD launch in H2 2026; median ~15,000 trackers per patient; R-squared >0.99

quarterly_data.signal: Other launches and pipeline: ChromoSeq, a heme therapy-selection assay using Whole Genome and Whole Transcriptome, launched on April 1, received MolDX coverage at a reimbursed rate of $3,228 and its first Medicare reimbursement. MI Clarity, a digital-pathology prognostic for early and late breast cancer recurrence risk, is live; version 2, adding chemotherapy and extended endocrine therapy decision support, launches in H2 2026. Caris is in the planning phase of an FDA submission for Caris Assure, its next submission; New York State approval is still in review and is not in guidance. The mutational-cleanse program follows a Detect signal with the Caris MAX assay at 10,000x depth of coverage and AI scoring of immunogenic mutations (83.8% positive predictive value and 86.5% sensitivity on the top variant per patient) to make personalized peptide immune targets.
quarterly_data.figure: ChromoSeq MolDX rate $3,228; Caris MAX 10,000x depth; PPV 83.8%; sensitivity 86.5%

quarterly_data.signal: Commercial: the sales realignment completed in January 2026 expanded territories from 82 to 146, with a further expansion underway; the field organization ended Q2 with more than 290 commercial team members (270 at the end of Q1) and surpassed 300 in July, with no plan to stop there. CFO: new reps typically take six to nine months to fully ramp, and added reps are not in guidance until KPIs play out. CFO on M&A: an acquisition would have to be additive to technology and capabilities, and nothing in the pipeline meets that bar now.
quarterly_data.figure: territories 82 to 146; >290 commercial team members (300+ in July)
